items.title: Examining K-2 Educators' Perceptions of Project Read AI in Developing Instructional Materials
items.abstract: This qualitative study examined K-2 early childhood educators' perceptions of Project Read AI, an artificial intelligence platform designed specifically to support phonics-based instruction aligned with the Science of Reading. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model, the study investigated both the perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness of the platform among six kindergarten through second-grade teachers at a suburban New York elementary school. Findings indicated that educators perceived the platform as generally user-friendly and expressed strong intentions to integrate it into their practice. Evaluations of instructional materials yielded mixed results: the Decodable Game was viewed as a highly effective engagement tool, the Lola Science of Reading chatbot produced lesson frameworks valued as supplemental resources, and the Decodable Text Generator showed instructional promise but required improvements. Implications are given for educator practice, professional development, and future research on AI-powered literacy tools in early childhood education.

items.title: Expanded Urban Innovation for the Twenty-Second Century: From Cutting Emissions to Enabling Flourishing Lives on a Thriving Planet
items.abstract: Cities are central to the climate challenge, but much research on urban climate action still focuses on emissions reductions within existing systems. This literature review assesses existing research and literature, including work on human-need-driven innovation for global sustainability and the export of globally sustainable solutions. Rather than limiting urban climate action to measures aimed at reaching zero emissions, the review examines an expanded urban innovation agenda in which cities are studied as incubators and exporters of innovations that support flourishing lives for all on a flourishing planet. The review synthesizes insights from sustainability transitions, sociotechnical systems, well-being economics, artificial intelligence, and brain science. Case studies from different cities illustrate how some urban innovation agendas are already shifting. The comparison highlights how a focus on flourishing lives can mobilize start-ups, youth, and public institutions, while addressing equity and positioning cities as actors in the next generation of urban climate action.

items.title: Experimental evaluation of the effect of the feed bowl design on the eating behavior of domestic cats in the context of whisker stress
items.abstract: Aim of the study. To evaluate the effect of feed bowl design on the eating behavior of domestic cats with emphasis on the phenomenon of whisker stress. Materials and methods. A prospective within-subject study with sequential exposure to two feeding conditions was conducted in 26 clinically healthy domestic cats. Animals were sequentially fed from a standard deep narrow bowl (control) and a wide shallow bowl (experiment) with a 3-day adaptation period. The following parameters were recorded: amount of feed consumed, amount of dropped feed, number of approaches to the bowl, presence of pauses and attempts to extract feed with a paw. Statistical analysis was performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Fisher's exact test and binomial test. Results. No statistically significant differences in feed consumption were found between the two conditions (p > 0,05). When using the wide shallow bowl, no feed dropping was observed (0%), whereas when feeding from the standard bowl, dropping occurred in 38,5% of cats (p < 0,05). In the preference test, cats did not show a preference for either bowl (p > 0,05). Behavioral markers of sensory discomfort were not recorded. Conclusions. Bowl design affects feeding ergonomics and the amount of spilled feed but does not confirm the existence of whisker stress as a systemic phenomenon in domestic cats. Recommendations for the use of wide bowls may be justified by practical considerations of convenience.

items.title: Expert evaluation of ChatGPT-generated responses to patient questions in conventional and fast-track total knee arthroplasty
items.abstract: Fast-track total knee arthroplasty (TKA) asks patients to understand early mobilization, early discharge, opioid-sparing analgesia, and selective use of drains and catheters. We evaluated expert-rated quality of ChatGPT responses to patient questions about these pathway-specific concepts alongside conventional TKA questions. In this cross-sectional evaluation, three arthroplasty surgeons independently scored responses to 50 conventional TKA and 20 investigator-developed fast-track questions in four domains on 5-point scales. The conventional questions were selected by a multidisciplinary panel; the fast-track questions did not undergo the same selection process. Response-level means were compared descriptively and with exploratory Mann-Whitney U tests. Seventy responses received 210 expert assessments. Recalculated mean ± SD scores across individual ratings were 4.99 ± 0.15 for accuracy, 4.98 ± 0.14 for completeness, 4.98 ± 0.17 for safety, and 5.00 ± 0.07 for readability. Each of the 20 fast-track responses received a score of 5 from each of the three raters in all four domains (Supplementary Table S1). Nevertheless, question-set construction differed and scores clustered at the ceiling, so the exploratory comparison does not establish equivalence. Experts gave high ratings to the evaluated responses, including those on fast-track concepts. The observed data do not establish equivalence between question sets: the fast-track ratings require source-data verification, the sets were selected differently, and scores were concentrated at the maximum. Clinician review remains appropriate for protocol-dependent and safety-related advice. Not applicable.

items.title: Explainability Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection from Genomic Data
items.abstract: Genetic disorders affect millions worldwide, posing major challenges for accurate diagnosis and effective treatments. New developments in genomic technologies, especially Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS), have enhanced the classification of genetic modification and improved diagnostic abilities. Moreover, the Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) methods emerged as efficient tools for evaluating the intricate genomic data and determining the patterns, which can be generally complex to identify by employing conventional analytical techniques. Additionally, the Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has developed as a significant constituent in the analysis of genomic data by enhancing the interpretability of DL methods and showing the contribution of main genetic features involved in the detection of genetic disorders. This study presents an Explainability-Aware Heterogeneous Temporal Graph Transformer for Automated Genetic Disorder Detection (XHTGT-AGDD) approach. The primary objective of the proposed model is to improve the reliability and accuracy of genetic disorder detection from genomic data by integrating advanced techniques. Initially, preprocessing is performed using quantile transformation to normalize the input data for robust analysis. Following preprocessing, feature selection is performed using the fire hawk optimizer to identify the most informative feature subsets from the genomic data. Besides, the classification task is accomplished using a heterogeneous temporal graph transformer, which captures complex relationships and temporal dependencies among genomic features. To further refine the learning process, hippopotamus optimization algorithm is employed for model optimization. In addition, an explainability mechanism based on SHAP is incorporated to interpret the model predictions and highlight the individual genetic features toward the final decision. The experimental result analysis of the XHTGT-AGDD model is performed using a benchmark dataset. The simulation results reported the enhanced results of the XHTGT-AGDD technique in terms of several measures, achieving an accuracy of 99.12%. Therefore, the proposed model provides reliable and effective performance for automated genetic disorder detection from genomic data.

items.title: Explainable AI-Driven Intelligent Video Summarization for Next-Generation Video Production and Content Management
items.abstract: This chapter reviews the development of video summarisation using handcrafted features and deep learning models, the recent advances in transformer-based, vision-language, multimodal learning, and large language models for video summarisation. It introduces the main steps of the summarization pipeline: keyframes extraction, keyshots generation, importance score prediction and summary generation. Particular focus is given to explainability techniques like LIME, Grad-CAM, attention maps and multi-granular explanations, and how frame, shot, semantic, and story-level explanations can help to increase the transparency and user trust. Applications in film and media production, OTT platforms, news, education and surveillance are also discussed as well as challenges concerning explainability evaluation, computational complexity, privacy, ethics and scalability. The future involves explainable LLMs, personalized summarization, human in the loop AI, interactive systems and foundation models.

items.title: Explainable deep graph attention learning with enhanced residual SwinV2 transformer for interpretable facial paralysis severity assessment
items.abstract: Facial paralysis is a severely disabling disorder that causes weakness or damage to facial muscles, thus leading to abnormal or asymmetric facial movements. Timely and precise detection and grading of facial paralysis is more essential for appropriate treatments and rehabilitations. Conventionally, facial image analysis was a manual process relying on expert proficiency. Recently, deep learning (DL) techniques have revolutionized the field, especially in the context of facial and clinical image analyses. While DL enables automatic, accurate facial recognition, its black-box nature restricts its use in healthcare. Therefore, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is integrated to enhance transparency that provides visual evidence for medical decision-making. This study introduces an Explainable Deep Graph Attention Learning Framework for Facial Paralysis Identification (XDGAL-FPI). The proposed model is designed to automatically identify the severity of facial paralysis using facial image data. Initially, the input images are preprocessed, including face detection and alignment, color space conversion and contrast enhancement, noise reduction, normalization, and data augmentation to improve the quality and consistency of the input data. Besides, deep feature representations are extracted using an Enhanced Residual SwinV2 Transformer. The extracted features are then provided to a Heterogeneous Graph Attention Network that models the relational dependencies between multiple facial regions, such as the eyes, eyebrows, and mouth, for precise severity classification. Additionally, to improve the training efficiency and convergence behavior of the model, the Ranger optimizer is employed. Furthermore, the GradCAM + + technique is integrated to improve model interpretability by highlighting the important facial regions that contribute to the model’s prediction. The effectiveness of the proposed model is assessed using YouTube Facial Paralysis (YFP) Updated Dataset, which contains 14, 389 images categorized into four severity levels across different facial regions. The experimental results indicate that the proposed XDGAL-FPI model achieves improved performance compared with existing approaches across various evaluation metrics. Thus, the proposed XDGAL-FPI model can serve as a reliable and interpretable tool for automated facial paralysis severity assessment. The source code of this study is available at https://github.com/researcher010-debug/XDGAL-FPI .

items.title: Explaining the Roles of Experts in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs for Personalization
items.abstract: Personalization of Large Language Models (LLMs) is increasingly important for user-centric applications, yet prior methods mainly adapt dense LLMs, whose polysemantic neurons, each encoding multiple unrelated concepts, hinder localizing the components behind personalization, and thus understanding and controlling it. We propose to personalize Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs, which sparsely route each token to a few specialized experts, reducing polysemanticity and enabling such localization. We adapt three open-weight MoE LLMs on a large-scale personalization dataset and train crosscoders on paired activations of the personalized and non-personalized models to learn interpretable personalized latents, from which we identify the experts encoding distinct personalization features. The personalized MoE LLMs perform competitively with dense LLMs while activating only a fraction of their parameters, exhibit lower polysemanticity than dense LLMs with similar active parameters, and, within the same model family, yield personalized latents that are less shared with the non-personalized model. Causal interventions show that these latents suffice to recover the personalized model's behavior and that boosting their associated experts moves the non-personalized model toward it, revealing distinct routing paths for different personalization features.

items.title: Exploring AI-resistant assessments: insights from Large Language Models creating and completing their own research assessments
items.abstract: Higher education institutions have been grappling with the impact of Large Language Models (LLMs) on teaching and learning. LLMs like ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek, can produce high-quality text with a single prompt. This is particularly concerning in research modules, where students are expected to showcase their work in a text-based format. In this study, ChatGPT, Claude, and DeepSeek were prompted to develop three research assessments that an LLM should not be able to complete and were subsequently prompted with the instructions generated. The purpose was to explore the influence of assessment instructions and characteristics on the ability of these models to generate complete responses. The instructions and characteristics included written text, oral discussions, physical attendance, contextual access, realistic content, lecturer approval, and the inclusion of multiple components. The most influential characteristic was the inclusion of an oral component. Other noteworthy characteristics were requiring students to attend live events and including multiple staged components. These findings contribute to the ongoing exploration of assessment design in the age of AI and LLMs.

items.title: Exploring Empowerment Challenges Facing SMMEs in the Nelson Mandela Bay Automotive Industry
items.abstract: Small, Medium and Micro Enterprises (SMMEs) play a critical role in South Africa's automotive industry by promoting economic growth, supplier development, and employment creation. However, persistent empowerment challenges continue to constrain their participation in automotive value chains and limit their contribution to youth skills development and workforce development pathways. This study aimed to explore the empowerment challenges facing SMMEs within the Nelson Mandela Bay automotive industry and to examine how these challenges influence opportunities for youth skills formation and sustainable workforce development. A qualitative case study design was adopted, employing purposive and snowball sampling to recruit 15 participants comprising SMME owners, Sector Development representatives, and Automotive Industry Development Centre (AIDC) officials. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analysed using six-phase thematic analysis. The findings identified six interrelated themes that constrain SMME empowerment: access and resources, skills and training, communication and information, policy and leadership, infrastructure and operations, and motivation and organisational culture. Collectively, these barriers restrict SMMEs' competitiveness, reduce their ability to participate in supplier development initiatives, and weaken their capacity to provide workplace learning opportunities, apprenticeships, and technical skills development for young people entering the automotive industry. The study concludes that strengthening institutional support, improving communication between stakeholders, expanding access to finance and infrastructure, and aligning empowerment initiatives with industry needs are essential to enhancing SMME sustainability and supporting inclusive workforce development. The study contributes to the growing body of knowledge on SMME empowerment by demonstrating the close relationship between enterprise development, youth employability, and regional workforce development within South Africa's automotive industry.

items.title: Exploring the role of green innovation and logistics in linking Logistics 4.0 to sustainable performance: why digitalisation alone is not enough?
items.abstract: The logistics sector operates as a complex sociotechnical system in which digital transformation and environmental sustainability interact as interdependent subsystems. Logistics 4.0 technologies are credited with improving operational efficiency, yet how they translate into performance remains underexplored within an integrated systems framework. Drawing on a systems science perspective, this study examines how Logistics 4.0 affects logistics performance directly and indirectly through green logistics and green innovation. Survey data from 338 manufacturing firms were analysed using structural equation modelling and mediation analysis. All seven hypothesised relationships were supported: Logistics 4.0 predicted green logistics (β = 0.735), green innovation (β = 0.631) and performance (β = 0.532), and both mediators predicted performance (β = 0.647 and 0.419). The mediating channels differ in magnitude: green logistics carries a strong indirect effect (k2 = 0.331) and green innovation a moderate one (k2 = 0.203), indicating that the operational and strategic routes to sustainable performance mature on different horizons. The study contributes by modelling these constructs as complementary subsystems rather than isolated variables, and by differentiating empirically the strength of the two mediating channels. For managers and policymakers, the implication is direct: digitalisation delivers its full return only when planned jointly with sustainability capability.

items.title: Extended Judgment: LLMs and the Architecture of Artificial Capacities
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded in everyday epistemic practices, yet their epistemological status remains unclear. Existing debates typically oscillate between treating LLMs as epistemic agents or reducing them to mere tools. This paper argues that both views mischaracterize the core issue. Drawing on a teleological interpretation of 4E cognition and the paradigm of human–AI coevolution, it develops an alternative account that understands LLMs as components of extended epistemic capacities, most centrally the human capacity for judgment. On this view, epistemic capacities are not intrinsic properties of isolated subjects or systems, but purposive and relational achievements enacted within sociotechnical practices. LLMs do not possess epistemic agency or original normativity; rather, they reshape the conditions under which human judgment, inquiry, understanding, and justification unfold. By analyzing language, coevolutionary feedback loops, derived normativity, and epistemic autonomy, the paper shows how epistemic responsibility remains human while epistemic performance becomes technologically extended.

items.title: Eye-Tracking for Cognitive Load Assessments in a Manufacturing Environment: A Feasibility Study
items.abstract: Maintaining cognitive load that is neither too high nor too low is key for workplace safety and efficiency. Cognitive load assessment research is often conducted in highly controlled laboratory environments that, by nature, come short of fully recreating the everyday manufacturing floors. In this feasibility study we explore the viability of adopting eye-tracker for assessing workers’ cognitive load as they complete seatbelt manufacturing assemblies in a factory workplace. Following the industrial partner’s availability, four assembly workers were selected for this feasibility study. They wore a portable Pupil Labs eye-tracker while completing seatbelt assembly tasks. Mental task demand was measured using subjective ratings. Results showed that the quality of the eye-tracking data was high in spite of the highly dynamic full-body motions required to complete assemblies. Also, no evidence was found that the presence of the eye-tracker interfered with task completion. Tasks deemed more mentally demanding were associated with greater pupil size and blink rate, a pattern consistent with laboratory research. Despite this study’s limitations, including its small sample size, these findings represent preliminary evidence for the adoption of eye-tracking metrics for conducting cognitive ergonomics assessments on factory floors.

items.title: Federated Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models (Fed-LLMs): Parameter-Efficient Adapters, Split Learning, and Gradient Privacy Bounds
items.abstract: Abstract—Fine-tuning Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision Foundation Models on private, decentralized domain data is essential for specialized healthcare, legal, and financial enterprise applications. However, centralizing domain-specific text corpora triggers catastrophic data privacy violations under stringent regulatory mandates (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA), while full-parameter federated fine-tuning incurs insurmountable communication bottlenecks (>140 GB per communication round for a 70B parameter model) and exhausts edge GPU memory. The confluence of Federated Learning (FL) and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT)—designated as Fed-LLMs—establishes a scalable paradigm where decentralized client nodes collaboratively adapt foundation backbones while sharing exclusively low-rank parameter updates. Nevertheless, deploying Fed-LLMs across heterogeneous edge infrastructures introduces severe systems challenges: non-independent and identically distributed (non-IID) catastrophic forgetting, communication bandwidth saturation over constrained wide-area networks, split learning intermediate activation leakage, and susceptibility to gradient inversion attacks in autoregressive attention layers. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical architectural evaluation of Federated Fine-Tuning for Foundation Models. We formalize federated low-rank adaptation (Fed-LoRA) aggregation under statistical distribution skew, derive the mathematical dynamics of Split Federated Learning (SplitFed) across partitioned transformer layers, and establish formal differential privacy bounds under DP-FedAvg. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise multi-node testbed comprising 64 distributed client nodes fine-tuning open foundation models (Llama-3-8B, Llama-3-70B, and Mistral-7B) across multi-tenant clinical records, financial reports, and legal jurisprudence. Our empirical findings demonstrate that quantized federated low-rank adaptation (Fed-QLoRA, rank r=8, 4-bit NormalFloat) reduces uplink communication payloads by 99.4% (from 14.2 GB down to 84 MB per round) while retaining 96.8% downstream domain accuracy compared to centralized full-parameter fine-tuning. Concurrently, activation obfuscation in SplitFed bounds reconstruction attacks to below 0.002 PSNR. Finally, we formulate open research directions in heterogeneous client rank adaptation, post-quantum secure aggregation, and federated alignment via decentralized direct preference optimization.

items.title: FedSkillGit: Federated Skill Evolution via Version Control
items.abstract: Large language model agents can improve their capabilities by evolving reusable natural-language skills from execution experience. In real-world deployments, this experience is distributed across data owners who cannot pool their raw data, which motivates federated skill evolution. The natural first design lets each client evolve the whole skill document and upload the result for server-side aggregation. That design is poorly matched to skill evolution for three reasons. An evolved document can still carry client-specific content distilled from private traces, repeated transmission of a nearly unchanged document spends communication on knowledge that the population already holds and the contribution of a single client is buried in a document that the server cannot meaningfully attribute. We propose FedSkillGit, a federated skill evolution framework that replaces full-document updates with commits. Each participating client submits a bounded set of patches over named rules together with its local experience, which summarizes what the round taught it, and the pair passes a two-stage privacy filter before it leaves the client. The server deduplicates the submitted patches and the local experience of all participants, updates a global experience document that only the optimizers read, and merges the surviving patches into a candidate skill. The candidate is distributed to the clients, which score it on their own validation sets and report the results, and it is published only when the reported scores improve on the current version. Experiments on three datasets and three language model families show that FedSkillGit outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by up to 22% and approaches centralized evolution without sharing raw client data.

items.title: Fine‐Grained Hybrid Attention‐Aware Deep Learning Framework for Automated Multi‐Layer Cyberattack Detection in IoT‐Cloud Environments
items.abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of Internet of Things (IoT) with cloud platforms has generated an extremely decentralized, data‐driven network that is transforming industries. At the same time, the integration poses intricate cybersecurity challenges because of scalability requirements, device heterogeneity, and an evolving threat environment. Conventional security metrics are inadequate in some circumstances, creating a necessity for adaptive, intelligent, and proactive defense modules. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers beneficial capabilities for intrusion detection, predictive threat modeling, anomaly detection, and malware analysis. Moreover, deep learning (DL) models have proved exceptional effectiveness in automatically learning intricate patterns from larger‐scale network traffic information, allowing precise identification of advanced cyberattacks in IoT‐cloud systems. Therefore, this manuscript presents a Fine‐Grained Hybrid Attention‐Aware Deep Learning Framework for Multi‐Layer Cyberattack Detection (FGHADL‐MLCD). The major intention of the proposed model is to enhance the reliability and intelligence of cyberattack detection in large‐scale IoT‐cloud infrastructures. The FGHADL‐MLCD approach operates through a sequence of stages, including preprocessing, attribute selection, cyberattack classification, and model optimization. Initially, the collected network traffic data from TON‐IoT and Edge‐IIoT datasets undergo preprocessing operations such as data cleaning, label encoding, feature scaling, and dataset splitting to ensure consistency of input data. Following that, an effective attribute selection mechanism is introduced using the Boruta feature selection technique, which identifies the most relevant network traffic features. For multi‐layer cyberattack detection and classification, the proposed model employs a bidirectional temporal convolutional network integrated with an attention mechanism. Furthermore, the training process of the deep learning model is optimized using the Adam optimizer. To assess the model's effectiveness, extensive experiments are conducted using the benchmark IoT cybersecurity datasets. The experimental results indicate that the proposed technique achieves improved cyberattack detection performance compared to recent models. Thus, the proposed model delivers a reliable solution for securing IoT‐cloud infrastructures against diverse and evolving cyber threats.

items.title: Firefighters’ Perceived Causes of Musculoskeletal Injuries: Identifying Modifiable Targets for Prevention
items.abstract: Musculoskeletal injuries are a major occupational health concern in the fire service and can affect firefighter health, operational readiness, staffing, and injury-related costs. Although prior research has described the epidemiology of firefighter injuries, less is known about how firefighters perceive the causes of musculoskeletal injuries. This study examined perceived contributors to musculoskeletal injury among 113 career firefighters from two Mid-Atlantic fire departments. Firefighters completed an open-ended survey question asking them to identify the top three reasons firefighters are injured on the job. Responses were analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis, and theme frequencies were summarized overall and compared across department, sex, age group, and years of service. Nine themes were identified. Insufficient physical fitness was the most frequently reported perceived contributor (75.2% of participants), followed by complacency or protocol non-compliance, fatigue and impaired sleep, improper movement technique, and limited mobility or flexibility. Perceived contributors were generally consistent across demographic and occupational subgroups. These findings suggest that firefighters perceive musculoskeletal injuries as largely related to modifiable individual and behavioral factors. Identifying firefighter-perceived causes of injury may help inform worksite prevention efforts, including fitness development, fatigue mitigation, movement education, mobility training, and reinforcement of safe work practices.

items.title: Following Delegation Traces to Study Human Oversight in Interaction with Multimodal AI
items.abstract: As multimodal AI systems are becoming our everyday thought partners, the shift towards studying how users transfer control to these systems becomes especially urgent. In this paper, we report an overview of findings from an online study with n=56 AI-literate participants and 392 Video Question Answering trials. After inspecting each multimodal AI response, participants rated task-specific trust and selected one of three intended policies for an analogous future task: reject AI assistance, use it with verification, or delegate fully to the AI. Within participants, post-interaction trust strongly predicted the user's delegation choices (OR=14.97, 95% CI [7.14,31.37]). Trust and delegation nevertheless remained distinct. Verification was the dominant policy and often co-occurred with high trust. Delegation also increased with task order after adjustment for momentary and participant-level trust (OR=1.22, 95% CI [1.02,1.45]), indicating an experience-related component that self-reported trust ratings alone could not capture. These findings motivate a shift from intended delegation to a non-intrusive observation of how delegation is enacted in collaborative human-AI tasks. We therefore conclude by proposing enacted delegation traces as a methodological framework for future studies of multimodal and agentic AI use.

items.title: ForTress: Bringing Assurance and Determinism for LLM-Driven Fortran-to-Python Translation
items.abstract: Modernizing mature scientific software from Fortran to Python can improve accessibility and integration with modern computing tools, but manual rewriting is expensive. Large language models (LLMs) make translation more practical, yet generated code can pass regression tests while violating source-language semantics, and contextual corrections may not persist across subsequent translations. We present ForTress, which solidifies recurring LLM translation decisions into guarded executable rules for deterministic reuse and provides semantic assurance for a non-trivial subset of these rules. Its LLM-assisted auditing process expresses universally quantified preservation obligations over mechanized Fortran and Python semantics in Lean. Human experts review semantic fidelity and correspondence with production rules, and Lean's kernel checks proofs and refutations under explicit assumptions. These audit records expose the conditions either supporting correctness or identifying failure cases. We evaluate ForTress on 17 benchmarks from 15 scientific software spanning diverse domains. The translated programs achieve bitwise-identical with native Fortran on all evaluated tests under the recorded execution and initialization configurations. Against these software, ForTress accumulates 193 executable rules and 188 audit records, of which 121 have checked soundness proofs, including 31 established after counterexample-guided refinement. Cross-software reuse exceeds 90% for 14 of the 15 software. Even with additional assurance and determinism, the LLM usage cost is 44.2% lower than direct LLM translation.

items.title: From Agro-Food By-Products to Precision Nutraceuticals: Bioactive Compounds, Molecular Mechanisms, Bioavailability and Clinical Translation
items.abstract: The valorization of agro-food by-products represents a potential strategy to address both environmental sustainability and the growing demand for innovative health-promoting products. Traditionally considered waste materials, agro-food residues are now recognized as valuable sources of bioactive compounds, including polyphenols, flavonoids, carotenoids, terpenoids, peptides, and other phytochemicals with potential nutraceutical applications. This review aims to provide a critical synthesis of the transition from agro-food by-product recovery to the development of evidence-based precision nutraceuticals. Particular attention is given to the chemical diversity of bioactive compounds obtained from representative agro-food sources, including citrus, olive, grape, tomato, and pomegranate residues, highlighting their biological activities and therapeutic potential. The molecular mechanisms underlying their health-promoting effects are discussed, focusing on key pathways involved in oxidative stress (Nrf2), inflammation (NF-κB), metabolic regulation (AMPK/SIRT1), mitochondrial homeostasis, autophagy/mitophagy, and apoptosis. Beyond the description of biological activities, this review critically addresses the main challenges limiting the translation of agro-food-derived bioactives into effective nutraceutical products, including bioavailability, bioaccessibility, intestinal metabolism, standardization of extracts, variability of raw materials, dose optimization, and the gap between preclinical findings and clinical evidence. The translational bottleneck is examined in detail, emphasizing the need for robust clinical validation and regulatory compliance. Finally, future perspectives are discussed, highlighting the potential of emerging technologies, including precision extraction, omics approaches, artificial intelligence, and personalized nutrition, to overcome current limitations and to enable the development of sustainable, safe, and effective nutraceutical interventions. By integrating advances in food science, molecular pharmacology, and human health research, this review provides a comprehensive perspective on how agro-food by-products can be transformed into scientifically validated nutraceutical platforms, supporting the development of sustainable and personalized strategies for disease prevention and health promotion. Despite promising preclinical evidence, clinical validation remains limited: most human studies are small, of short duration, and none have evaluated hard clinical endpoints.

items.title: From AI-Based Market Forecasting to Investment Strategy
items.abstract: This chapter examines the role of artificial intelligence in transforming market analysis and investment strategy through machine learning-based stock direction forecasting. It proposes a standardized and reproducible evaluation framework that integrates predictive modeling, cross-firm robustness assessment, and risk-adjusted economic evaluation within a unified methodology. Using five large-cap technology firms as an empirical illustration, the chapter demonstrates how machine learning-generated market signals can support investment decisions and be evaluated using predictive accuracy, cumulative returns, Sharpe ratio, and maximum drawdown. The findings indicate that ensemble learning methods, particularly XGBoost, provide more robust predictive signals and superior risk-adjusted performance across multiple firms. The chapter emphasizes methodological rigor, economic validation, and cross-firm consistency, providing a practical framework for AI-driven financial forecasting and investment decision support.

items.title: From Answer Generator to Questioning Coach: Designing AI-Assisted Coaching for Self-Regulated Learning in Higher Education
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support self-regulated learning (SRL), but its pedagogical value depends on whether interaction elicits learner cognition or substitutes for it. This study examined how students’ reported use of GenAI corresponded to an intended question-first coaching design, the perceived processes and tensions associated with SRL, and conditions relevant to potential scale. A qualitatively driven embedded case study utilized 31 reflective portfolios as the primary dataset, complemented by 53 survey responses and 68 weekly logs from 12 maximum-variation cases. Abductive, reflexive thematic analysis generated five themes. Question-led interaction appeared most useful when it prompted problem reframing, led to a bounded evidence-producing action, and preserved learner judgment through evaluation, modification, or rejection of AI suggestions. Benefits were qualified by role drift, generic interaction, cognitive substitution, uneven engagement, and continued need for human support. The findings support a distributed coaching-system interpretation in which AI-supported elicitation, pedagogical scaffolding, learner agency, reported AI-role configuration, and function-specific human support interact. The study does not demonstrate institutional scalability; instead, it identifies scale-relevant conditions including sustained engagement, manageable scaffolding, role boundaries, safety, learner judgment, and routes to human expertise.

items.title: From Bare to Informed Looking: An Art-Historical Proposition on Mindful Art Engagement, Emotion Regulation, and Cognitive Enrichment in the Age of AI
items.abstract: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence has unsettled more than the labour market. It has given rise to two related anxieties: an existential unease about human meaning, agency, and uniqueness—“AI anxiety”—and a quieter abdication of critical effort to machines, which recent works call “cognitive surrender.” The remedies most often proposed for these conditions, among them psychoeducation, regulation, engineering ethics, and therapy, leave a conspicuous gap, since none of them draws on aesthetic experience or on the making of meaning. This article, written from an engaged, applied art-history position, proceeds as a conceptual analysis rather than an empirical study. It defines “mindful art engagement” as a receptive, two-phase practice that moves from bare to informed looking, an open and contemplative looking followed by art-historically informed interpretation, sets out its boundaries, distinguishes the three constructs on which it bears (felt meaningfulness, art-historical understanding, and cognitive enrichment), and maps the existing evidence onto its components. On this basis, it advances a hypothesis that such a practice could contribute to emotion regulation and to cognitive enrichment in the age of AI, and that meaning is the point at which the two pathways meet.

items.title: From Classrooms to Smart Campus Management with Web 3.0 Tools
items.abstract: Throughout history, humans have continuously developed and experienced advanced technologies designed to automate labor-intensive processes and streamline herculean tasks. Currently, our generation is actively harnessing the multi-faceted power of Web 3.0 technologies, which are characterized by their comprehensive, all-around attributes. Key innovations such as artificial intelligence, virtual reality, augmented reality, extended reality, blockchain, non-fungible tokens, smart contracts, decentralized platforms, and intelligent learning management systems represent the vanguard of these uprising Web 3.0 tools and platforms. While these technological advancements profoundly elevate major industries including business, finance, medicine, and agriculture, they also critically upgrade our academic field. Web 3.0 tools do more than just elevate the standard teaching and learning experiences; they actively organize and manage entire college and university academic ecosystems, providing the most seamless operational experience available. By deploying these tools, college administrations can effortlessly handle multiple complex tasks simultaneously, consistently resulting in perfect project completion and execution. This paper outlines the strategic utilization of Web 3.0 tools and platforms within the respective sectors of colleges and universities to demonstrate a measurable betterment of workflow within institutional management. From immersive virtual classrooms to decentralized campus management systems, Web 3.0 tools play a vital role in redefining the professional responsibilities of academic staff, professors, students, research assistants, lab instructors, librarians, and administrative assistants. Furthermore, this paper exhibits the implementation of Web 3.0 technologies across other crucial academic dimensions, specifically highlighting research development, secure student data management, and peer-to-peer (P2P) collaboration.

items.title: From conversation to green intention: how perceived AI chatbot empathy shapes sustainable travel
items.abstract: Recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI) have expanded the role of conversational agents in hospitality and travel service encounters. However, it remains unclear how the conversational characteristics of AI become psychologically meaningful and relate to travelers’ sustainable decision-making. Drawing on Cognitive Appraisal Theory (CAT), this study examines the associations between Chatbot Conversational Quality (CCQ) and Green Travel Intention (GTI) through the sequential roles of Perceived Chatbot Empathy (PCE) and Green Travel Motivation (GTM), while considering Eco-Friendly Customer Innovativeness (EFCI) as a boundary condition. Survey data from 400 travelers show that CCQ is associated with PCE, which in turn is associated with stronger GTM and, subsequently, higher GTI. EFCI strengthens the PCE-GTM relationship but does not significantly moderate GTM-GTI, suggesting greater relevance during motivation formation than motivation-to-intention translation. The findings show how conversational AI interactions can acquire socio-emotional meaning in hospitality contexts and highlight customer heterogeneity in sustainability-related decisions.

items.title: From Counterfeit Detection to Supply Chain Resilience: How Converged Digital Trust Technologies Secure Third-Party Logistics Supply Chains
items.abstract: Counterfeit goods create economic, security, and sustainability risks for supply chains, yet blockchain, radio-frequency identification (RFID), and artificial intelligence (AI) have mostly been studied as separate technologies. This study conceptualises their joint adoption as Logistics Anti-Counterfeiting Digital Technology (LACD) adoption, a converged capability combining identification, traceability, and analytical detection. Drawing on Rational Choice Theory and Deterrence Theory within a perspective informed by the Technology-Organisation-Environment framework, it examines the antecedents and outcomes of LACD adoption and the moderating role of government regulation. Survey data from 232 medium and large third-party logistics (3PL) firms in China were analysed with partial least squares structural equation modelling. Perceived benefit, deterrent severity, and deterrent certainty were positively associated with LACD adoption, whereas perceived complexity and cost were negatively associated with it; sanction celerity was not significantly associated with adoption. LACD adoption was positively associated with logistics security effectiveness and supply chain resilience. Government regulation strengthened the effects of perceived benefit, deterrent severity, and deterrent certainty and weakened the negative effect of perceived cost, but did not moderate the effects of perceived complexity or sanction celerity. The study also proposes, as an untested proposition, that LACD may provide traceability infrastructure for circular supply chain practices.

items.title: From Dyadic Reciprocity to Giant Interaction Engines
items.abstract: In this paper, based on posthumanist theory and posthumanist linguistics, we discuss specific elaborations of the term interaction as found in linguistics and sociology, where interactivity, reciprocal awareness and agency are discussed as possible characteristics of human interaction. We problematise to what extent this is distinct from interaction between humans and machines. We bring these discussions in relation to illustrative observations on how users of ChatGPT report on their experiences with large language models, drawn from Reddit threads. We show that the concept of interaction is ‘under construction’, not only because we have new interactional partners but also because meaning-making is now intertwined with the changing and individually customised and at the same time collectivised media affordances of machine-learning technologies. Interaction is no longer perceived as typically taking place between two humans but as embedded in and distributed across time and space in large networks of speaking subjects, massive historical and ever-changing data sets, and algorithmic affordances.

items.title: From groups to teams: applying Team Academy methodology in organisational development
items.abstract: Purpose Team Academy, known in Finnish as Tiimiakatemia, is a well-known method for team-based learning in education, but rarely studied as a tool for organisational development (OD). This article asks whether Team Academy methodology can help organisations move from groups to genuine teams, and whether human collective learning will become a key organisational strength as artificial intelligence changes what individuals can do. Design/methodology/approach The article combines a literature review, drawing on the learning organisation (Senge), knowledge creation (Nonaka and Takeuchi) and selfmanaged learning (Cunningham), with three semi-structured interviews. The practitioners interviewed had each introduced Team Academy methodology inside a large organisation: an industrial technology and logistics company, a telecommunications company and a financial services company. The three cases are discussed together, theme by theme, using thematic analysis. Findings Thematic analysis identified eight cross-case themes, including person-dependent adoption, partial uptake of Team Academy tools, letting go of hierarchical control and middle management as a friction point. Rather than one shared model, the cases show a repeating pattern: a committed individual applies parts of the methodology, meets resistance and builds trust through small steps. A six-phase framework is proposed. Originality/value Team Academy methodology has been widely studied in education, but very little academic work has looked at its use in OD. This article addresses that gap using original practitioner interviews from three sectors, and connects Team Academy to a topic not previously explored: artificial intelligence in the workplace. The resulting six-phase framework offers a new, practical starting point for organisations and researchers.

items.title: From Natural Language Intent to Executable Control: Hierarchical Feedback-Guided LLM Planning for Multi-component Cyber-Physical Systems
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, two gaps hinder their use for real execution: generated plans may misinterpret or omit the user's intent, and even a logically plausible plan may be infeasible under component dynamics, interactions, or safety constraints. Existing LLM-based planning approaches often lack informative feedback on why a generated plan fails, providing little guidance for revising the plan accordingly. To address these challenges, we present a hierarchical feedback framework that uses different types of feedback information to guide LLMs in generating executable plans for CPSs. We prompt LLMs to generate both a structured task plan and corresponding signal temporal logic (STL) constraints, and design a sound algorithm that identifies definite contradictions between them and provides feedback for revising inconsistencies. At the execution level, when control synthesis fails, we extract different types of diagnostic information, such as violated constraints and conflicting component assignments, and feed them back to guide task replanning. Experiments on seven heterogeneous multi-component CPS scenarios have shown that our framework can generate executable plans and feasible control executions that satisfy the original natural language missions with a success rate of 87.9% with GPT-5.

items.title: From need satisfaction to academic achievement: pathways through wellbeing and engagement among university students across different Italian institutions
items.abstract: Background University students face personal and academic demands that may challenge their adaptive functioning. Although intrinsic goals, need satisfaction, wellbeing, and academic engagement have been distinctively linked to academic achievement, an integrated model specifying how these constructs are structurally related and associated with students' academic outcomes is lacking. The present study addresses this gap by testing models grounded in Self-Determination Theory and previous evidence. Methods Participants were 2891 university students ( M age = 23.22 years, SD age = 5.25 years; 74.75% women) recruited across multiple Italian universities. The online survey comprised different measures, including socio-demographic items, the Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale, the Aspiration Index, the SInAPSi Academic Engagement Scale, and the Mental Health Continuum-Short Form. Structural equation modeling was used to test two alternative model specifications. Starting from a more general model, progressively more parsimonious models were tested by constraining selected direct effects. The final model was selected based on comparative fit, overall model fit, parsimony, and theoretical coherence. Results The retained model specified wellbeing as antecedent to academic engagement. Within this model, basic psychological need satisfaction showed indirect links to academic achievement through wellbeing and academic engagement, while intrinsic goals were related to achievement only through academic engagement. Academic engagement emerged as the most proximal predictor of achievement, mediating the pathways from need satisfaction, intrinsic goals, and wellbeing. Conclusions These findings provide an integrated account of how satisfaction of basic psychological needs, intrinsic motivations, wellbeing, and academic engagement relate to academic achievement in university students. Our evidence supports a model in which psychological need satisfaction represents a relevant condition associated with wellbeing, intrinsic goals contribute more specifically to academic engagement, and academic engagement acts as the proximal mechanism linking these factors with academic achievement. Beyond advancing theoretical understanding, our results may inform preventive programs and interventions nurturing students' wellbeing while also promoting their academic performance.

items.title: From Observation to Intervention: Distilling Self-Generated In-Context Demonstrations via Executable Causal Intervention
items.abstract: Self-generated In-Context Learning (ICL) enables LLMs to synthesize their own few-shot demonstrations, often outperforming manual prompts. However, existing methods filter demonstrations by observation, assuming a rationale is high-quality if it leads to the correct output. We show such filtering suffers from \textit{observational equivalence}, whereby both faithful causal rationales and spurious post-hoc rationales can yield same outputs and are statistically indistinguishable from observation alone. Inspired by independent causal mechanisms, we argue that faithful rationales imply \textit{transfer invariance}, in which causal rationales should remain effective across logically similar samples. We instantiate this criterion as \textbf{E}xecutable \textbf{C}ausal \textbf{I}ntervention for \textbf{D}emonstrations \textbf{D}istillation (ECI2D), which abstracts language rationales into executable programs and applies the causal interventions ($do$-operator) on logically similar samples, retaining only those demonstrations that imply transfer invariance. Experiments on math, logical and commonsense reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that ECI2D consistently outperforms observation-based ICL while retaining far fewer demonstrations, with gains exceeding 7 points as the test distribution shifts.

items.title: FROM PIXELS TO PROMPTS: A STRUCTURED NARRATIVE REVIEW OF SECURITY, PRIVACY, AND ADVERSARIAL ROBUSTNESS IN HEALTHCARE AI
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in healthcare, where evaluations usually ask whether a system is accurate on ordinary clinical data. This review asks instead what can happen when someone deliberately changes the data, instructions, or training to make a system fail, behave in hidden ways, or reveal confidential information, a field known as adversarial machine learning. We reviewed 113 publications (2018–2026) and grouped the reported threats into six categories: altering an input after training; corrupting the training examples; teaching a hidden rule triggered later; using the model to learn private information; placing malicious instructions in language or image-and-language models; and attacking models trained jointly across hospitals or devices. Laboratory studies showed that small deliberate changes to medical images could alter a diagnosis or a model's outline, corrupted training data could change what a model learned, and malicious prompts could produce unsafe medical responses. Effect sizes varied greatly across models, datasets, attacks, and test conditions. Several defenses helped in individual experiments, but no single defense was shown to work across all threats and settings; in one imaging study, attacks tailored to the tested defenses bypassed all five. The studies do not show how often these attacks occur in practice or harm patients; their value is to demonstrate possible failure modes under controlled conditions. Medical AI should therefore be evaluated both on ordinary clinical data and in clearly described, clinically plausible attack scenarios.

items.title: From Signals to Evidence: Interpretable Underwater Acoustic Target Sensing with Large Language Models - Part I: Framework and Recognition
items.abstract: Underwater acoustic target detection and recognition are essential to marine surveillance and intelligent ocean sensing. Despite substantial advances in deep learning, existing systems typically produce binary detection decisions, categorical labels, or scalar confidence scores, offering limited insight into the physical evidence underlying their outputs. Large language models (LLMs) offer an opportunity to move underwater acoustic sensing toward interpretable, evidence-grounded understanding; however, generic audio encoders struggle to capture the distinctive physical characteristics of underwater acoustics, and physically annotated data are scarce. In this paper, the first of a two-part series, we propose a from-signals-to-evidence framework that integrates physics-aware acoustic encoding with a pretrained LLM, organized around a unified feature-evidence-decision chain with a shared reasoning core. An open input layer accommodates heterogeneous information-raw waveforms, time-frequency representations, environmental and geographic data, and textual physical priors-unifying detection and recognition within a common formulation. In Part I, we instantiate this framework for target recognition through an Underwater Acoustic Physics-aware Transformer (UPT), which tokenizes complementary acoustic representations and learns task-disentangled physical representations through four physics-oriented learning tasks. We develop a physics-parameterized data engine that provides traceable supervision at two levels of granularity and introduce an attribute-level evaluation protocol to assess the physical fidelity of generated descriptions. Experiments on simulated recordings of four vessels demonstrate accurate vessel recognition and reliable estimation of shaft frequency, blade-passing frequency, and machinery-related attributes.

items.title: From Single-Modal Signal Recognition to Multidimensional Precision Detection: Breakthroughs and Innovations of Multi-Modal Sensors in Tumor Biomarker Detection
items.abstract: The sensitive detection of tumor markers is of great significance for clinical diagnosis. Due to the extremely low abundance of early tumor biomarkers and severe background interference from biological matrices, traditional single-modal atomolar biological testing generally has limitations such as high false positives and narrow linear ranges, making it difficult to meet the clinical needs of precise diagnosis and treatment. This has driven the iterative development of biosensing technology from a single signal readout mode to multi-modal collaborative analysis, significantly improving the sensitivity and accuracy of complex biological sample detection. Dual-modal sensors integrate two complementary sensing mechanisms, whereas multi-modal sensors produce three or more independent signal outputs. By combining such mechanisms, for example electrochemistry and optics, these platforms can establish a signal cross-validation and self-calibration detection system. This multidimensional analysis strategy can mitigate interference caused by environmental factors and human operational errors to a certain extent, lowering detection limits and broadening the linear range, thereby potentially providing higher-reliability data support for early tumor diagnosis. This work systematically reviews the technological evolution and performance differences in tumor biomarker sensors from single-mode to multi-mode in recent years, with a focus on summarizing the cutting-edge research progress in this field. It provides a comprehensive reference for researchers and facilitates further applications of multi-modal sensors in point-of-care detection, and artificial intelligence-assisted analysis.

items.title: From skills to smart care: The mediating role of digital literacy in the relationship between digital competence and medical artificial intelligence readiness among nursing students
items.abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare requires nurses to possess strong digital competence, advanced digital literacy, and readiness to engage with AI technologies. Despite this need, the ways in which digital competence influences AI readiness, and the mediating role of digital literacy, remain underexplored. This descriptive cross-sectional study examined 500 undergraduate nursing students from two Universities for Health Sciences in Saudi Arabia and Egypt using validated measures of digital competence, digital literacy, and medical AI readiness. Results indicated strong positive correlations between digital competence, digital literacy, and AI readiness, with digital literacy partially mediating the effect of digital competence on AI readiness. These findings highlight the importance of integrating ethical, reflective, and AI-focused digital literacy alongside technical skills in nursing education, ensuring that future nurses are prepared to use medical AI effectively and safely, thereby supporting clinical decision-making and improving quality of care.

items.title: From Theory Architecture to Political Orientation: The Development and Research Programme of Jean-Pol Martin's Zenodo Corpus
items.abstract: This conceptual working paper maps the development of Jean-Pol Martin’s Zenodo corpus from the reconstruction of an integrated theoretical architecture toward political orientation and accountable action.The analysis identifies five overlapping strands: conceptual integration; anthropological and epistemic clarification; historical grounding; societal knowledge integration; and political application. Learning by Teaching (LdL) provides a participatory learning process, the New Human Rights (NMR) articulate six basic needs as normative concerns, and human–AI cooperation supports synthesis and conceptual work under human responsibility.The paper’s specific contribution is a developmental map connecting these strands and explaining the recent emphasis on political responsibility, democratic cooperation, ecological conditions of life, and the protection of victims of aggression. It offers a seven-text reading route and proposes a research programme addressing historical source verification, comparative assessment, documented applications, and AI-supported judgment.Within the series, the article serves as an updated orientation document following the June 2026 overview, “Jean-Pol Martin’s Zenodo Corpus as an Open Book.”The supplied search listing reports 50 records. The analysis draws on selected titles, abstracts, and publication metadata provided by the author; it is not a full-text review of all 50 publications and presents no new empirical dataset.Jean-Pol Martin supplied the theoretical framework, source listings, and conceptual direction. ChatGPT assisted with synthesis, English drafting, and PDF preparation. Responsibility for the published text remains with the human author.

items.title: From Tool to Pedagogy
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping education across sectors, yet its adoption often remains tool-focused rather than pedagogically grounded. This chapter argues for reframing AI as a pedagogical innovation informed by established learning theories and frameworks. Drawing on constructivism, sociocultural theory, connectivism, cognitive load theory, self-determination theory, Universal Design for Learning, TPACK, SAMR, Activity Theory, and human-centered AI, it presents a synthesis for meaningful and ethical integration. The discussion highlights AI's implications for instructional design, learner agency, equity, and assessment, while critically examining tensions around personalization, surveillance, automation, and professional autonomy. By advancing a theory-driven perspective, the chapter provides educators, researchers, and policymakers with a structured lens to evaluate AI's transformative potential beyond technical functionality.

items.title: From Trajectories to Experience: A Survey of Experience-Driven LLM Agents
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can plan, use tools, and recover from errors within a task, yet many carry little from one task to the next and repeat mistakes they have already resolved. The root cause is a lack of experience accumulation: trajectories record what failed and how the agent recovered, but this information is seldom turned into guidance for later tasks. Research on this capability spans reflection, agent memory, workflow learning, and skill acquisition, but these lines describe similar content in different terms and lack a common account of experience itself, leaving basic questions open: what counts as experience, how it should be accumulated, used, and revised, and how to tell whether it improves later behavior. This survey addresses these questions with a unified framework. We define agent experience as action-guiding information grounded in task trajectories and retained to guide later episodes where it applies, whether as a trajectory precedent, a semantic lesson, or a reusable procedure. We focus on explicitly accessible experience, including its use as a training signal for internalization into model parameters. We describe each unit of experience by its guidance, applicability conditions, execution evidence, and reliability evaluation, so that memory entries, workflows, and skills become directly comparable, and follow experience through four lifecycle functions---formation, organization, utilization, and maintenance---that determine how it is accumulated, used, and revised. To judge reported gains, we distinguish three improvement claims---fixed experience reuse, feedback-driven sustained improvement, and improvement of the learning mechanism---by the evidence each requires. Current studies most clearly support fixed experience reuse, chiefly on tasks with tests or reference answers; evidence for the other two claims remains partial. Our analysis yields recommendations for seven application settings and a central design principle: keep guidance connected to its applicability conditions and to the evidence that supports or challenges it. Finally, we outline eight open problems, from learning with human expert records to testing whether gains accumulate, toward agents whose improvement is cumulative, transferable, and correctable.

items.title: Full-Duplex Interaction with Speech, Expressions and Gestures
items.abstract: Human face-to-face conversation requires coordinating speech, gestures and expressions across both speaking and listening. We present ELLSA 2, an end-to-end full-duplex dialogue model that jointly optimizes speech interaction and streaming gesture-expression generation. An autoregressive, chunk-wise synthesizer combines pretrained acoustic features with distinct listening and speaking hidden states from the dialogue backbone and speech synthesizer, enabling continuous non-verbal generation even when the model is verbally silent. To translate dialogue understanding into vivid semantic gestures, we introduce contextual semantic calls and template guidance, separating whether to invoke an available semantic gesture from how to realize it. We also establish a curated data and evaluation pipeline for dialog-aware co-speech gesture generation and investigate reference-based multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as automatic judges. Experiments show that ELLSA 2 remains highly competitive with open-source full-duplex speech interaction models and outperforms cascaded baselines across dialog-aware gesture and expression metrics. Semantic template guidance further significantly improves semantic gesture quality. Strong system-level correlations with human judgments support these reference-based scores as useful preliminary metrics for full-duplex and semantic gesture assessment. Together, these results advance dialogue modeling from spoken responses toward coordinated multimodal interaction.

items.title: Functional Subnetwork Localization for Efficient Continual Learning in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Biological intelligence continually adapts to new information while retaining prior skills through localized plasticity. In contrast, continual learning in large language models (LLMs) remains vulnerable to catastrophic forgetting. A promising direction is to identify functionally specialized subnetworks within LLMs that enable targeted and resource-efficient adaptation. Using gradient-attribution profiling, we localize cognition-associated functional subnetworks exhibiting extremely low mutual overlap. Building on this finding, we propose Function-isolated Memory-Efficient Optimization (CiMEO), a continual learning framework that routes each training example to its corresponding functional subnetwork, restricting parameter updates and optimizer states to selected regions. Across 1.4 million sequential instructions, CiMEO achieves the highest average performance among the compared methods on five generative benchmarks spanning programming, examination-style tasks, and mathematical reasoning, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. Subspace-overlap and principal-angle analyses further indicate that localized updates help preserve pre-trained representations, highlighting functional subnetwork localization as a practical approach to efficient and stable continual learning in LLMs.

items.title: Future Directions and Policy Implications of Artificial Intelligence in Higher Educational Institutions
items.abstract: With the advent of artificial intelligence, technology has advanced significantly in recent years. In this regard, artificial intelligence has the potential to play a role in higher education institutions in accelerating sustainable development. This chapter discusses global artificial intelligence policies and current debates in formulating them. As artificial intelligence tools become more accessible, educational institutions increasingly need to develop artificial intelligence education policies that equip students with the necessary knowledge and skills. Several countries have policies around using artificial intelligence in higher education institutions. Regarding this, the present chapter mainly aims to understand the future directions of artificial intelligence in higher education institutions in developed, developing, and underdeveloped countries and the main policy issues surrounding artificial intelligence and ethical codes that can ensure artificial intelligence and that support human rights

items.title: Fuzzy Kano Validation of Generative AI-Curated Features for Simponia Redesign
items.abstract: Background: Generative AI (Gen AI) has accelerated UX design processes, yet no systematic protocol exists to validate AI-curated features against actual user preferences before prototyping. Objective: This study applies the Fuzzy Kano Model as a validation checkpoint for Gen AI-curated features in the redesign of Simponia, a web-based portfolio and community management platform at Universitas Muhammadiyah Malang. Methods: An exploratory mixed-methods case design was used. Claude Opus generated 36 feature candidates from a Structured Requirements Document and ISO/IEC 25010 criteria. Fuzzy Kano validation involved 87 Informatics students; fuzzy membership and the Last of Maxima classification method were used to determine Kano categories, while weighted scoring was retained only for post-classification prioritization. Results: No features were classified as Must-be or One-dimensional (maximum Must-be membership degree = 0.073). Eleven features (30.6%) were classified as Attractive, and 25 (69.4%) as Indifferent. Triangulation indicated that 58.3% of features were in Quadrant 2, suggesting a misalignment between AI-based technical evaluation and actual user preferences. Sixteen features (44.4%) were flagged as ambiguous (Δμ < 0.10). Conclusion: The Fuzzy Kano Model demonstrates potential as a validation checkpoint by exposing systematic divergence between AI curation and user preferences, with a Quadrant 2 (Q2) rate of 58.3%, indicating the importance of user validation following autonomous AI-assisted feature curation in resource-constrained educational contexts.

items.title: GACC-Bench: Benchmarking Goal-Adaptive Context Compression Ability across Large Language Models
items.abstract: Context compression in long-running applications of large language models (LLMs) must preserve goal-relevant information, often before specific downstream questions are known. We introduce GACC-Bench, a benchmark for Goal-Adaptive Context Compression that evaluates how reliably LLMs adapt information retention to specified high-level goals. For each source context, we derive one or more high-level goals by grouping source-grounded questions according to shared downstream objectives. The benchmark contains 500 goals and 2,571 questions over 281 document and agent-trace contexts from seven collections spanning diverse domains, with all instances reviewed by human experts. The compressor receives a source context, a goal, and a context-length budget, with the associated evaluation questions withheld. A fixed reader answers these questions individually using the same compressed context. Our evaluation of ten LLM compressors reveals substantial gaps to full-context performance even for the best-performing model, particularly in supporting correct answers to every question associated with a goal. Compared with goal-agnostic compression, target-goal conditioning consistently improves accuracy, whereas mismatched-goal conditioning reduces it. GACC-Bench is available at https://github.com/weiting24/GACC-Bench.

items.title: Game-Based Learning Experience and Occupational Health and Safety Learning Achievement: The Mediating Role of Learning Engagement in Vocational Training
items.abstract: Occupational health and safety is a mandatory component of public vocational training; however, lecture-based instruction may not sufficiently engage adult learners. This study examined the effect of the game-based learning experience on learning achievement, with learning engagement as a mediating variable, among occupational health and safety trainees at the South Jakarta Regional Job Training Center, Indonesia. A quantitative explanatory survey was conducted with all 174 participants enrolled in the 2026 Batch 1 regular and Mobile Training Unit classes using saturated sampling. All participants completed a game-based learning session on the Wayground platform, formerly known as Quizizz. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire adapted from established instruments and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The game-based learning experience had a positive and significant effect on learning engagement (β = 0.854, p < 0.001) and learning achievement (β = 0.592, p < 0.001), while learning engagement had a positive and significant effect on learning achievement (β = 0.343, p = 0.016). Learning engagement partially mediated the effect of the game-based learning experience on learning achievement (indirect effect = 0.293, p = 0.017). The model explained 72.9% of the variance in learning engagement and 81.6% of the variance in learning achievement. Approximately one-fifth of participants reported technical barriers, primarily unstable internet connections, system lag, device limitations, and game time limits perceived as too short. The findings suggest that game-based learning activities can enhance learner engagement and perceived learning achievement in occupational health and safety training for adult vocational learners, provided that adequate technical readiness is ensured.

items.title: GENERATIVE AI AND EFL WRITING: ITS IMPACT ON ACCURACY, COMPLEXITY AND FLUENCY
items.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has significantly influenced second and foreign language education, particularly the teaching and learning of writing. Generative AI tools such as ChatGPT can provide immediate feedback, generate ideas, suggest vocabulary, revise grammatical structures, and support learners throughout different stages of the writing process. However, the extent to which AI-assisted writing contributes to learners’ actual linguistic development remains an important research question. This conceptual paper examines the potential impact of GenAI on three central dimensions of English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing performance: accuracy, complexity, and fluency (CAF). Drawing on recent research in second language writing and AI-assisted language learning, the paper analyzes the benefits and limitations of GenAI for each dimension. The literature suggests that AI-assisted writing can contribute particularly to grammatical accuracy and lexical sophistication by providing immediate corrective feedback and exposure to alternative linguistic forms. Evidence concerning syntactic complexity and writing fluency, however, is less consistent. Although learners may produce more polished and fluent-looking texts with AI assistance, this does not necessarily indicate corresponding development in their independent writing ability. The paper therefore argues that the pedagogical value of GenAI depends largely on how learners interact with the technology. When used as a supplementary writing assistant rather than a replacement for independent production, GenAI can support language development, learner autonomy, and reflective writing practices. The paper concludes by proposing pedagogical principles for responsible AI integration into EFL writing instruction and identifying directions for future empirical research.

items.title: Generative AI in Accounting Policies and Estimates: Safeguarding Professional Judgment and Addressing Managerial Bias
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used in corporate reporting, where accounting policies and estimates require professional judgment. The central risk examined is not automated error but automated advocacy: a fluent, standard-referenced justification for a preferred treatment can now be obtained in seconds, making biased judgment a governance problem before it is an accounting problem. Using theory adaptation, this conceptual study integrates research on professional judgment, motivated reasoning, and automation reliance. It identifies five bias-amplification mechanisms: anchoring, automation bias, outcome-directed prompting, unverified justification, and diffusion of responsibility. It develops TRACE, a proposed framework comprising task boundary, regulatory grounding, alternative assessment, challenge and contradiction, and evidence trail. Its intended operation is illustrated using four constructed IFRS cases (IAS 8/IAS 16, IAS 36, IAS 37, IFRS 15) and a boundary-condition variant in which TRACE does not resolve the disagreement. The AI proposals are stylised illustrations, not model outputs or empirical data. GenAI appears most defensible when used to generate alternatives and challenge a preferred treatment, and least defensible when asked to select or justify a conclusion. TRACE may make AI-assisted judgments more attributable and contestable, but it has not been empirically validated and cannot guarantee unbiased outcomes.
